Rashi on Niddah 5a:10:1.english: It does not reduce - [neither] with regard to [the period of] a twenty-four-hour period, and with regard to [the period] from examination to examination:

Rashi on Niddah 5a:11:1.english: Since she is excited for her husband - She hurries to have relations.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:12:1.english: One for him - That he wipes himself with it.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:14:1.hebrew: ותחפנה שכבת זרע - ואפי' דלאחר תשמיש נמי לא ליהוי כפקידה, קמ"ל:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:14:1.english: And semen covered it - And even [an examination] after intercourse should also not be [considered] like a [valid] examination; [therefore the mishna] teaches us [otherwise].

Rashi on Niddah 5a:15:1.hebrew: ואי בעית אימא - לעולם חד לפני תשמיש וחד לאחר תשמיש, ואפ"ה "הרי זו כפקידה" אלאחר תשמיש קאי. וא"ת עד שלפני תשמיש, למה הוזכר מתניתין? תרתי קתני, ואשמועינן תנא דמתניתין דשני בדיקות אצרכוה רבנן. וה"ק "משמשת בעדים", כלומר מצוה עליה לשמש בעדים, ואע"פ שיש לה וסת, "הרי זו כפקידה" ההוא דלאחר תשמיש:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:15:1.english: And if you wish, say - Actually, [the Sages required] one [examination] before intercourse and one after intercourse, and nevertheless "it is like an examination" refers only to the one after intercourse. And if you ask: [If so,] why was the one before intercourse mentioned in the mishna? [The answer is that] it teaches two things, and the Tanna of the mishna informs us that the Sages required two examinations. And this is what it means to say: "she engages in intercourse with examination cloths" — that is, it is a mitzvah for her to engage in intercourse with examination cloths, even if she has a set cycle; "it is like an examination" — that is, the one after intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:15:3.hebrew: תני ומשמשת - ותרתי מילי נינהו. וה"ק: מצוה עליה לשמש בעדים, והרי היא כפקידה אבתרא, וקמא לא נקט ליה אלא לאשמועינן דמצוה לבדוק קודם תשמיש:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:15:3.english: Teach: "and she engages in intercourse" - They are two separate matters. And this is what [the mishna] is saying: It is a mitzvah for her to engage in intercourse with examination cloths, and [the act] is like an examination with regard to the latter [examination, i.e., after intercourse]. The first [examination] it mentioned only to teach us that it is a mitzvah to examine before intercourse.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:16:1.hebrew: השתא מעת לעת - דאתמול, דזמן ארוך הוא, ממעטת פקידה זו את הזמן דעדים:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:16:1.english: Now, [if it reduces] from a twenty-four-hour period - [Which is a period] of yesterday, which is a long time, this examination reduces [the time] of examination cloths:

Rashi on Niddah 5a:2:1.hebrew: ולוקמא איפכא - כדאוקמיה מעיקרא. ומ"ט הדרי בה? הא שפיר מצי לאוקמי מתני' כדברי הכל, וברייתא כרבנן:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:2:1.english: But let us interpret it the opposite way - As we interpreted it originally. And what is the reason that they retracted from it? Surely we can well interpret the mishna [as in accordance with] everyone, and the baraita [as in accordance with] the Rabbis:

Rashi on Niddah 5a:3:1.hebrew: לקולא ולחומרא - מעיקרא אוקימנא לקולא, דבשעת וסתה דברי הכל דיה שעתה, ובשלא בשעת וסתה פליגי. והשתא אוקימנא פלוגתא בשעת וסתה, ואיכא דמחמיר ומטמא לה למפרע, ושלא בשעת וסתה ד"ה מטמאה למפרע:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:3:1.english: As a leniency and as a stringency - Initially we interpreted it as a leniency: that at the time of her fixed menstrual period, all agree that [her impurity applies only] from her present moment onward, and they disagree [only] about [blood discovered] not at the time of her period. But now we have interpreted the dispute as applying [even] at the time of her period, and there is one who is stringent and renders her impure retroactively, and [blood discovered] not at the time of her period — all agree that she is impure retroactively.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:4:2.hebrew: שאם תראה כו' - אלמא דטעם דכתמה מטמא למפרע, משום דאשכחן בהו ראייה טמאה למפרע. דהשתא, לא הוה כתמה חמור מראייתה. וש"מ, דאשה דיש לה וסת הוא דפלוג רבנן בין כתמה לראייתה: דכתמה מטמא למפרע, ובראייתה דיה שעתה. משום דבראייתה שלא בשעת וסתה אשכחן טומאה למפרע:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:4:2.english: "For if she sees," etc. - Evidently, the reason that her blood stain renders [her] impure retroactively is that we find in [such cases] that a sighting renders [her] impure retroactively; for otherwise, a blood stain would not be more stringent than her sighting. And we learn from this that it is [only] with a woman who has a fixed cycle that the Rabbis distinguished between her blood stain and her sighting: that a blood stain renders [her] impure retroactively, whereas with her sighting, [it is enough that she is impure] from her [own] time onward. This is because [in a case of] her sighting not at the time of her fixed cycle, we do find retroactive impurity.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:1.english: Their stains are like their sightings - From this point onward, they are impure.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:2.hebrew: חוץ מתינוקת כו' - דאפילו מכאן ולהבא נמי לא. והא דאמר לעיל בתולת דמים כתמן כראייתן, דמכאן ולהבא מיהא טמאה — היינו כשהגיע זמנה לראות ולא ראתה:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:2.english: Except for a young girl, etc. - For even from now onward, [her stain is] also not [impure]. And that which [the Gemara] said [earlier] that a "virgin of blood," their stains are like their sightings, so that from now onward at least she is impure — this is [speaking of a girl] who has reached the time to see [blood] but has not seen.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:3.hebrew: מלוכלכין בדם - ולא ידעה אי אתי מגופה אי לא:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:3.english: Soiled with blood - And she does not know whether it came from her body or not.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:4.hebrew: אין חוששין לה - ואפילו אין לה במה לתלות, דבשוק של טבחים לא עברה איכא למימר עברה ולאו אדעתה, דהא בגופה אין לתלות כל עיקר. דכתמין דרבנן נינהו, וכי גזור רבנן בהגיע זמנה דדם מצוי בה, אבל בהא לא גזור, הואיל ואין בה דמים. ולקמן מפרש איזה הוא זמנה: משיגיעו ימי הנעורים, שהביאה שתי שערות, או בת י"ב שנה ויום אחד, ואע"פ שלא הביאה שתי שערות:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:6:4.english: One need not be concerned for her - Even if she has nothing on which to attribute [the stain], since it can be said that she did not pass through the butchers' market — [or] that she did pass through, but did not take notice — for [the stain] cannot be attributed to her body at all. For [the laws of] blood stains are rabbinic, and the Rabbis decreed [concern] only once her time has arrived, when blood is common in her; but in this case they did not decree, since there is no blood in her. And later [the Gemara] explains what her time is: from when the days of youth arrive, [meaning] when she has brought forth two hairs, or [when she is] twelve years and one day old, even though she has not brought forth two hairs.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:7:1.hebrew: ומי אית ליה לרבי חנינא כתם כלל - הכתם טמא בארבע נשים, ואפילו מכאן ולהבא:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:7:1.english: And does Rabbi Ḥanina hold [that there is] a stain at all - [that a stain is impure] in the case of the four [categories of] women, even from here onward?

Rashi on Niddah 5a:8:1.hebrew: דמחמיר בכתמים - טפי מבראייתה, דראיית ארבע נשים, הואיל ואין דם מצוי בהן, אמרינן: השתא אתי, ומכי אתי חזיתיה. אבל בכתם, איכא למימר: אי בדקה לחלוק מעיקרא, הוה אישתכח:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:8:1.english: For he is stringent with regard to stains - More than with regard to her seeing [blood] directly. For with the seeing of the four [categories of] women, since blood is not common among them, we say: It has only now come, and she saw it from when it came. But with a stain, one can say: Had she examined the garment initially, it would have been found [earlier].

Rashi on Niddah 5a:9:1.hebrew: רבי חנינא בן אנטיגנוס אומר נשים שאמרו חכמים דיין שעתן כתמן כראייתן - כלומר, נשים שאמרו חכמים דיין שעתן כתמן כראייתן, לטמאה מכאן ולהבא:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:9:1.english: Rabbi Chanina ben Antigonus says: Women regarding whom the Sages said, their time is sufficient; their stains are like their sightings - That is, women regarding whom the Sages said, "their time is sufficient; their stains are like their sightings," [this is] to render [them] impure from now onward.

Rashi on Niddah 5a:9:2.hebrew: יש לה כתם - מכאן ולהבא, אע"פ שלא ראתה מימיה:
Rashi on Niddah 5a:9:2.english: She has [impurity from] a stain - From now on, even though she has never seen [blood] in her life.

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:15:1.hebrew: תני ומשמשת - אף על פי שאמרו: דיה שעתה:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:15:1.english: Teach: "And she who engages [in intercourse using examination cloths]" - Even though they said: "It is sufficient for her [to be impure from] her time [of seeing the blood]":

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:16:1.hebrew: השתא מעת לעת ממעטת - פירוש: השתא מעת לעת, דפשעה ולא בדקה שחרית, כי בדקה ערבית ומצאה טמאה, בדיקה של צהרים דלאחר תשמיש מיעטה דלא מטמאה מעת לעת — כל שכן כשבדקה שחרית ולא פשעה כלום, דממעטת דלא מטמאה משחרית:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:16:1.english: Now, it reduces from a twenty-four-hour period - Explanation: Now, [if with regard to] a twenty-four-hour period, where she was negligent and did not examine in the morning, [and] when she examined in the evening and found herself impure, the examination of midday that followed intercourse reduced [the period], so that she does not become impure retroactively for the full twenty-four hours — all the more so when she examined in the morning and was not negligent at all, [it is obvious] that it reduces [the period], so that she does not become impure from the morning:

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:1:1.hebrew: וברייתא דברי הכל - דשלא בשעת וסתה מטמא למפרע, אבל לגמרי לא. אתי כרבנן, דלדידהו אפי' בשעת וסתה נמי. וא"ת: מעיקרא מאי סבר דאמרי' איפכא, ולא אמרי' לחומרא? ויש לומר: דמעיקרא בעי לאוקומי מתניתין ככ"ע; אבל כשהביא הברייתא, לא מצי לאוקמי ככ"ע, הדר ביה וקאמר לחומרא:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:1:1.english: "And the baraita is [the view of] everyone" - [This is because the baraita holds that] when it is not at the time of her expected period, she renders impure retroactively, but not [for the entire period] completely. [The Gemara's suggestion] accords with the Rabbis, for according to them, even at the time of her expected period, [she is impure retroactively] as well. And if you ask: At the outset, what did [the Gemara] hold, such that it said the opposite, and did not say [that the Mishnah is] stringent? One can answer: At the outset, it sought to establish the Mishnah as [following] everyone; but when it brought the baraita, it could not establish [the Mishnah] as [following] everyone, so it retracted and said [that it is] stringent:

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:5:1.hebrew: הא שאר נשים שאמרו חכמים דיין שעתן כתמן כראייתן - משמע שיש להחמיר ביש לה וסת טפי מבד' נשים. א"כ ר' דוסא, דאמר ביש לה וסת דיה שעתה, כל שכן דאית ליה בד' נשים! וקשה, דא"כ לקמן (נדה דף ז:) דפסיק כרבי אליעזר בד', אמאי חשיב הך בהדייהו? כיון דרבי דוסא סבר כותיה, לא ה"ל למיחשב, דכה"ג אמרינן לקמן. וי"ל, הא דביש לה וסת כתמה טמא למפרע, לאו משום דחמיר טפי מד' נשים, אלא משום דגזור בשעת וסתה אטו שלא בשעת וסתה, אע"ג דבראייה לא גזרינן:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:5:1.english: "Those other women, regarding whom the Sages said: Their time is sufficient; their stains are like their sightings" - This implies that one should be more stringent with a woman who has a set cycle than with the four women. If so, Rabbi Dosa, who said that with a woman who has a set cycle "her time is sufficient," certainly holds this for the four women! And it is difficult: for if so, later (Niddah 7b), where [the Gemara] rules like Rabbi Eliezer regarding the four [women], why does it count this one together with them? Since Rabbi Dosa holds like him, it should not have counted [it], for in a similar case we say later. And one can answer: The fact that a woman with a set cycle [whose] stain [is found] is impure retroactively is not because it is more stringent than the four women, but because [the Sages] decreed regarding the time of her cycle on account of [a time] that is not the time of her cycle, even though for a sighting we did not decree.

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:8:1.hebrew: ר"מ היא דמחמיר בכתמים - פירש"י: דמחמיר בכתמים טפי מבראייה. ואין נראה, דא"כ מה לו להש"ס להאריך ולומר "דמחמיר בכתמים"? הוה ליה למימר "ר"מ היא דתניא וכו'" ולא יותר. ותו, דבסמוך תניא: הרואה כתם — מקולקלת למנינה, וברואה דם — אינה מקולקלת למנינה. אלמא שאר תנאים נמי אחמירו טפי בכתמים מבראייה. ואע"ג דהך ברייתא כר"מ, דקתני "מטמאה את בועלה למפרע", ובפרק כל היד (לקמן נדה דף טו.) אמרינן דוקא לר"מ מטמאה בועלה למפרע — מכל מקום הא דמקולקלת למנינה מיהו אתי ככ"ע. וכן שילהי בא סימן (לקמן נדה נג:) תניא: הרואה כתם מטמאה עצמה למפרע בקדשים, והיינו לענין שמקולקלת למנינה, כמו שאפרש שם בע"ה. ונראה לפרש: רבי מאיר היא דמחמיר בכתמים — שהוא רגיל להחמיר בכתמים טפי מרבנן, כדתנן פרק בא סימן (נדה נב:): הרואה כתם חוששין משום זוב, דברי ר"מ; וחכמים אומרים: אין בכתמים משום זוב. ואמרי' התם: מאן חכמים? ר' חנינא בן אנטיגנוס, דמיקל יותר בכתמים, כדאמרינן הכא. ובכמה דוכתי מחמיר ר"מ, כדאמרינן לקמן (נדה דף נט:) גבי אשה שעושה צרכיה. ובפרק כל היד (לקמן נדה דף יד.) אמרינן: בדקה בעד [שאין] בדוק לה, והניחה בקופסא, ולמחר מצאה עליו דם — ר"מ מטמא, וחכמים מטהרין. ולכך קאמר הכא: ר"מ דמחמיר בכתמים. ואע"ג דבפ' האשה (לקמן נדה דף נט.) תניא: השאילה חלוקה לנכרית — אינה תולה בנכרית; ר"מ אומר: תולה בנכרית, אלמא מיקל טפי מרבנן — מ"מ ברוב מקומות מחמיר:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:8:1.english: "It is Rabbi Meir, who is stringent with regard to stains" - Rashi explained: that he is stringent with stains more than with [actually seeing] blood. But this does not seem right, for if so, why would the Talmud need to elaborate and say "who is stringent with stains"? It should have said, "It is Rabbi Meir, as it is taught, etc." and no more. Furthermore, shortly below it is taught: A woman who sees a stain — her count is disrupted, whereas one who sees blood — her count is not disrupted. Evidently the other *tanna'im* too were more stringent with stains than with [seeing] blood. And although that *baraita* follows Rabbi Meir, as it teaches that she "renders her husband impure retroactively," and in the chapter Kol Hayad (below, Niddah 15a) we say that only according to Rabbi Meir does she render her husband impure retroactively — nevertheless, the ruling that her count is disrupted accords with all opinions. And likewise at the end of [the chapter] Bo Siman (below, Niddah 53b) it is taught: A woman who sees a stain renders herself impure retroactively with regard to sacred foods, and that is with respect to her count being disrupted, as I will explain there, with God's help. And it appears to explain: "It is Rabbi Meir, who is stringent with stains" — in that he is accustomed to be stringent with stains more than the Rabbis, as we learned in the chapter Bo Siman (Niddah 52b): One who sees a stain, we are concerned that it is *zov*, the words of Rabbi Meir; but the Sages say: Stains do not carry the status of *zov*. And we say there: Who are the Sages? Rabbi Ḥanina ben Antigonus, who is more lenient with stains, as we say here. And in several places Rabbi Meir is stringent, as we say below (Niddah 59b) regarding a woman who relieves herself. And in the chapter Kol Hayad (below, Niddah 14a) we say: If she examined with an examination cloth that had not been inspected [for her], and placed it in a box, and the next day found blood on it — Rabbi Meir deems her impure, and the Sages deem her pure. Therefore it says here: Rabbi Meir, who is stringent with stains. And although in the chapter [entitled] Ha'ishah (below, Niddah 59a) it is taught: If she lent her garment to a gentile woman, she may not attribute [a stain] to the gentile woman; Rabbi Meir says: She may attribute it to the gentile woman — evidently he is more lenient than the Rabbis — nevertheless, in most places he is stringent:

Tosafot on Niddah 5a:8:2.hebrew: כל הנשים כתמן טמא למפרע ונשים שאמרו כו' - לא זו אף זו קתני:
Tosafot on Niddah 5a:8:2.english: "All women, their stains are impure retroactively, and women about whom [the Sages] said, etc." - The baraita teaches "not only this, but even this" [i.e., it states a progression: not only ordinary women, but even those for whom the Sages said "their time is sufficient"]:
